word-dice.def: small cubes with dots on each side, thrown to get a random number

word-roll-dice.def: to throw small numbered cubes onto a table to see what number comes up

word-turn-game.def: the time when one player is allowed to act before the next player

word-round-game.def: one complete stage of play in which every player acts once

word-card-game.def: a pastime in which players use a set of printed paper rectangles

word-deck.def: a full pack of 52 playing cards

word-shuffle.def: to mix playing cards so that their order is random

word-deal-cards.def: to give out cards to each player at the start of a game

word-draw-card.def: to take a card from the top of a pile during a game

word-discard.def: to lay down an unwanted one from your hand during a game

word-hand-cards.def: the playing cards that one person holds in a game

word-game-board.def: the flat surface with marked squares or paths on which a tabletop contest is played

word-board-game.def: a contest played on a table where pieces move across a marked surface

word-game-piece.def: a small object that a player moves or places during play

word-token.def: a small flat object used to mark position or score in a game

word-pawn.def: the smallest and weakest chess piece, which moves forward one square at a time

word-chess-king.def: the most important chess piece; if it is trapped, the match is lost

word-chess-queen.def: the strongest chess piece, which can move any distance in any direction

word-bishop.def: a chess piece that moves diagonally and has a pointed top

word-knight.def: a chess piece shaped like a horse that moves in an L shape

word-rook.def: a chess piece shaped like a tower that moves in straight lines

word-check-chess.def: a position in which a player's most important piece is under attack

word-checkmate.def: a position in chess where the king cannot escape, so the match ends

word-move-game.def: an action a player takes when it is their time to play

word-loser.def: a person who does not win a contest

word-bluff.def: to make others believe you have better cards than you really do

word-strategy.def: a careful plan for winning a game or reaching a goal over a long time

word-tactic.def: a specific action planned to gain a small advantage soon

word-hearts.def: the suit of playing cards marked with red shapes like a love symbol

word-diamonds.def: the suit of playing cards marked with red shapes like tilted squares

word-clubs.def: the suit of playing cards marked with black shapes like three-leaf clovers

word-spades.def: the suit of playing cards marked with black shapes like pointed leaves

word-ace.def: the playing card with a single symbol, usually worth the highest or lowest value

word-joker.def: an extra playing card with no suit that often acts as a wild card

word-trump.def: a playing card of a suit that beats all the other suits in a round

word-poker.def: a card game in which players bet on who has the best hand

word-dominoes.def: a game played with small rectangular tiles marked with dots

word-backgammon.def: a two-player game of racing pieces around a board after throwing dice

word-go-game.def: a two-player East Asian strategy game with black and white stones on a grid

word-mahjong.def: a Chinese game for four players using decorated tiles

word-checkers.def: a two-player game with round pieces moved diagonally across a board with squares

word-miniature.def: a small painted model of a person or creature, used in tabletop battle games

word-expansion.def: extra content sold separately that adds new rules or pieces to a game

word-rulebook.def: a printed manual explaining how to play

word-timer.def: a device that counts down seconds and minutes and signals when it reaches zero

word-game-night.def: an evening when friends or family meet to play tabletop pastimes

word-set-up.def: to arrange all the pieces and materials before play starts

phrase-your-turn.def: said to tell another player that it is now their time to act

phrase-whose-turn.def: asked when players are unsure who should act next

word-pass-turn.def: to choose not to act and let the next player go ahead

word-trade.def: to give an item to another player and get something else in return

word-resource.def: a material, such as wood or gold, collected and spent during play

word-quiz.def: a short test of what people know, often done for fun

word-trivia.def: small facts and details about many subjects, often asked as questions

word-riddle.def: a tricky question with a clever, surprising answer
